segments.text: “So, this is about last month, as you already know.
I do a 21-day challenge every month,
and during that challenge, I follow a morning routine with my community members.
Just like we usually follow the routine, I followed it as well, and one thing we
do every time after finishing the routine is that I talk to three people.” “That’s
where people ask their questions or share their stories,
and something very interesting happened on 14th August 2025.
When I went live, there was a person named Praveen Kumar.
He said, ‘Hello everyone, my name
is Praveen Kumar, and I am from Kalahandi, Odisha.
I am probably alive today only because of the Seeken channel.’”
“So, this happened 9 years ago.
Praveen Kumar had fallen from the stairs, and because of that, bleeding
started in his brain, which led him to go into a coma.
After going into a coma, he didn’t really know what was happening with him.
One thing he did find out after coming out of the coma was that all the money his
family had was completely gone.”
“The doctors had
said that surgery was necessary, and if it wasn’t done, he wouldn’t survive.
Unfortunately, since they
didn’t have the money, the situation was such that it seemed he might not live.
The doctor had told them that he had only about 10–15 days left, after which
his chances of survival would become
very slim.” “When Praveen found this out, he became very depressed — obviously.
But during
this time, he used to watch Seeken videos even before this incident, and that’s
when he came across a Seeken video titled How to Stop Worrying and Start Living.
In that video, I had explained how you can face your fears.
He started watching that video, and he found it incredibly inspiring.” “He found
it so inspiring that he started watching that video on loop again and again.
For one or two days — in fact, he says that whenever he felt really
low, he would watch that video, and it would give him inspiration again.
It gave him the courage to believe that maybe things would get better — and
guess what, things did get better.
Today, it has been nine years since that incident.”
“He is perfectly fine now, healthy, and living a good, fulfilling life.
And honestly, this story really inspired me.
It reminded me that the work we are doing —
the work of creating book summaries — is not just about book summaries.
It might actually be a source of hope.
It’s something through which I not only earn but also improve my own
life.” “It might even be saving some people’s lives.
So, for me, that was a very inspiring and proud moment.
And the video that helped
make all of this possible — today, I want to share that same video with you again.
Because honestly, once when I attended a YouTube event,
they asked me which one of my videos I would call my favorite or the best.”
“I had recommended this very video back then, saying that
everyone should watch it at least once in their lifetime.
And to be honest, I didn’t even know this story back then.
But there is definitely some kind of power
in this video — something I felt even when I created it.
And even today, whenever I watch it, I can still feel that same power.”
“You will definitely feel it too.
That’s why I want you to watch the same video — in the same style, with
my old voice, once again — and then tell me yourself whether you liked it or not.
Hey friends, no matter how rich, famous, or powerful we become, as long as
we worry too much about things, life will never feel as good as it should.
Overthinking creates stress, depression, anxiety,
and many other things that are not good for us at all.”
“Both mentally and physically — and after experiencing all these issues, even
if we were to get all the good things in the world, we still wouldn’t feel good.
Napoleon and Helen Keller are perfect examples that prove this point.
Napoleon had everything a
normal person dreams of — fame, power, money — everything.
Yet, on the island of Saint Helena, Napoleon admitted that he hadn’t spent
even six days of his life happily.” “Meanwhile, at the same time, Helen
Keller — who was blind, deaf, and mute — declared that life is very beautiful.
Now, if Helen Keller could live happily for 78 years
without worrying, then why can’t we, even with all our problems?
Overthinking has a huge impact on us.
Alexis Carrel, a Nobel Prize winner,
said that people who do not know how to fight worry die early.
Dr. O.F.
Goberon, a chief physician, also confirmed this.” “They explained that 70 percent
of patients who visit physicians could actually heal themselves
if they simply got rid of their fear and worry.
In one study, fifteen thousand patients were examined.
Among those who had stomach disorders, it was found that for four out of every
five patients, there was no physical reason for their illness; instead, their
fear, worry, hatred, and selfishness were the actual causes.” “Many famous doctors
say that stomach ulcers — which can be life-threatening
— heart disease, certain types of headaches, insomnia, and some types
of paralysis all have no other cause; they are simply caused by over-worrying.
Now, all of this should be more than enough for you to understand just how
harmful worrying can be for us.” “A magic formula for solving worrying situations.
Willis H. Carrier was an engineer.
Once, he got a project to install gas-cleaning devices in a
factory, a project that cost the company millions of dollars.
But after completing the project, Carrier realized that the devices he had
installed were not able to fulfill the guaranteed promises made to the company.”
“As a result,
the responsibility for a loss of millions of dollars fell entirely on Carrier.
He became extremely worried about this failure.
He worried so much that he couldn’t sleep.
But then his common sense reminded him that worrying wouldn’t fix the situation.
So, he came up with a technique to deal with his problem of worry,
and this technique turned out to be so effective that he still uses it today.”
“This technique has been around for more than thirty years
and consists of three simple steps, which you should also remember.
Step one: without fear and with complete honesty, find out what could
happen to you in the worst-case scenario because of this problem.
When Carrier thought about this, he realized that because of his
failure, he wasn’t going to go to jail or be executed.” “But
yes, his reputation in the market would be badly affected, and the 20 million
dollars he had invested with his employees would be completely lost.
Step two: once you know the worst-case scenario, mentally accept it.
Carrier told himself, ‘Okay, if this happens, it’s fine.
I will work hard again
to rebuild my reputation and explain to my employees that this was the
cost of our experiment to clean the gas.’” “After accepting the worst-case
scenario, Carrier felt an immense relief, something he hadn’t felt in a long time.
Step three: once the worst has been mentally accepted, think about
how you can make that worst situation better or improve it.
Again, after accepting the situation, Carrier started thinking about
how he could minimize the loss of those 20 thousand dollars.”
He conducted several tests and found out that if he invested
an additional five thousand dollars into his devices, they would work properly.
So, he did exactly that, and the result was that instead of a
20 thousand dollar loss, he made a profit of 15 thousand dollars.
After finding this solution, Carrier said that if he hadn’t followed these three
steps and had just kept worrying, he would never have achieved such a result.
“This technique is very useful for us too, because once you accept the worst
outcome, your mind stops jumping from one worry to another and can
concentrate more on solving the problem.
And until you accept your problem, your
mind will keep tormenting you, and no positive outcome will come.”
“Now, if some people feel that Carrier’s problem wasn’t that big and that
their own life problems are much bigger, here’s another true story for them.
A man named Earl P.
Honey had a duodenal ulcer.
Even the doctors, including specialists, had told Honey that there was no cure for
his disease and that his survival was impossible.” “Just imagine what
he must have gone through hearing this.
He became very distressed.
But then he decided that since he had very little
time left, why not spend it completely worry-free, happily, and live fully.
His dream was to go on a world tour before he died.”
“So that’s exactly what he decided to do.
He booked a ticket on a ship.
The doctors warned him that if he went, he wouldn’t be able to return and that
his body would have to be buried at sea.
Honey wanted to be buried in his hometown of Nebraska, so he took
his coffin with him.
He gave it to the ship’s crew and made an agreement that if
he died during the trip, they would bring his body back.”
“After making this arrangement, he went on the trip completely worry-free.
He ate and drank whatever he wanted without thinking, smoked big cigars,
played games, made new friends, and stayed up all night having fun.
He sang songs, enjoyed storms that were life-threatening, and when
the trip finally ended and he returned, he had gained 90 pounds in weight.”
“He completely forgot that he even had a stomach ulcer — surprisingly,
he became completely healthy.
After that, he went on to live a happy and healthy life.
Here, Honey used the same technique that Carrier had used.
He identified the worst possible outcome of his problem, accepted it, and then went
on the trip, trying to improve his situation a little.” “He
did all this without worrying.
Now, if after finding out that he was going to die
he had just kept worrying, the doctors’ words would have come true.
But he ended his worry and enjoyed life — and that saved his life.
Count your blessings.
Suppose someone comes to you and offers you ₹5 crore and says, ‘Sell me both
of your hands.’ Would you sell them?” “If that person gave you another ₹5 crore and
said, ‘Give me both of your legs too,’ and then offered even more money and
said, ‘Give me your eyes, your ears, and other body parts,’ would you give them?
As far as I think, hopefully you wouldn’t — and neither would I.
This shows us how rich we already are.” “We already own things that are
worth far more than crores — our health, our body, and our time.
But still, the thought-provoking part is that in order to own materialistic
things worth just a few lakhs, we put these most precious assets
under extreme pressure, punish them, and end up ruining them completely.”
“I’m not saying that you shouldn’t think about becoming successful, but pay
enough attention
so that in the pursuit of success, you don’t ruin your health and body.
Because no matter how big the success is, without health, it’s of no use.
We shouldn’t feel sad about the things we don’t have, but instead,
we should feel good by thinking about all the good things we already have.”
“This is a principle that has made my life much easier.
Whenever I start worrying about something, I remind myself that at the same time,
there are people somewhere whose entire family might be in danger of being killed.
There are also many people who are thirsty and don’t have clean water to drink.”
“There are also so many people who are starving so badly that they are eating
dirt to fill their stomachs.
And here I am, being so selfish, feeling sad worrying about my small problems.
We all get frustrated with life because of our problems.
But believe me, no person who knows
that today might be the last day of their life would spend it complaining.”
“If you were to tell that person, ‘Take my life along with all its problems,’ they
would gladly take all your problems and still be the happiest person in the world.
If you want to stay away from anxiety, stress,
depression, or worry, develop one habit: at least once a day, try to count
all the good things in your life and thank the higher power for them.”
“When you do this, you will realize how rich you already are in your mindset.
Don’t allow yourself to get upset over small things.
Robert Moore said this when he was trapped in a submarine 276 feet underwater.
It was wartime.
Japanese mine layers were attacking,
and at any moment, they could have taken his life.” “Seeing death
up close, he began to reflect on how he used to worry about small things.
When he had worked at a bank, long hours, low salary, not owning a home, not being
able to buy a car — all of these seemed like the biggest problems in life.
But now, facing death, he realized how trivial those worries were.
At that moment, he promised himself that if he survived, he would
never worry so much again.” “About anything, never.
He got that chance, survived, and after that, he
never broke his promise to himself of not worrying.
About all the worries we worry about — they never actually happen.
500 years ago, Michel de Montaigne said, ‘My life is full of troubles — troubles
that never actually happen in reality.’” “Research has
shown that 85% of the things we worry about never actually happen,
and of the 15% that do happen, 79% aren’t even worth worrying about.
This means that a total of 97% of the things you worry about
are nothing more than fears created by your mind that are troubling
you.” “So now I’ll tell you some ways to eliminate unnecessary worrying.
One of them is to keep yourself as busy as possible.
Because no matter
how smart a person is, they cannot think about two things at the same time.
So, when you start staying busy, you won’t even have time to worry, and you’ll
stay productive as well.
“Engage in work that uses your creativity and planning.
Another thing you can do is to think and act cheerfully.
Just as we cannot do two tasks
at the same time, we also cannot feel two emotions at the same time.
This means you cannot be extremely excited about one thing and,
at the same time, extremely sad about something else.”
“Whenever you feel tense, smile and act as if you are happy.
Doing this will actually make you start feeling good.
Because we cannot directly control our feelings, but we can control our actions
— and the good thing is that your actions and feelings are connected.
So when you act like you’re feeling good, you will actually start feeling good.”
“I shared this concept with you from Dale Carnegie’s book How
to Stop Worrying and Start Living, which has literally made the lives of millions
of people easier by eliminating stress, worry, and depression.
So, that was my video.
I hope you liked this video, and if you have any similar story — maybe you watched
one of my old videos that inspired you so much that it changed your life.”
“Because you know, on the same 14th of August, another person shared a story
about how until last
year, they didn’t have any money to give their sisters for Raksha Bandhan.
But a year later,
they earned so much that they were able to gift their sisters iPhones.
If you have any interesting stories like this, I would definitely love to hear
them.” “If you want, you can comment, or you can send your story
to this email ID and also mention the video that might have helped you.
That way, I can recreate or re-share that video in a creative new way so
that the same old value reaches people in a fresh style.” “For now, that’s all.
Thanks for watching.”
